transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
Lately I keep thinking about death, and I’m starting to worry about the thoughts I’m having about not wanting to be here anymore. It’s really starting to scare me, which is why I decided to come in.
I'm really glad you reached out for help today. Have these difficult feelings been triggered by a specific stressful event or major change in your life recently?

Yes, things got much worse about three weeks ago when I found out I failed a key certification exam for my RN-to-BSN program. I was already completely burnt out from working extended shifts at our understaffed clinic after a really rough hurricane season. Failing that exam just felt like my breaking point, making me feel like I'm failing my patients and my entire future.
Have you ever had times in your life where you felt the opposite of depressed—like having bursts of unusually high energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling extremely 'high' or wired for days?
No, I have never felt that way. I’ve never experienced periods of unusually high energy or felt 'high' or wired like you described.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless nearly every day, or have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy?

Yes, for about three weeks now I've been waking up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest and feeling completely hollow, just going through the motions. I've also lost all interest in things I used to love, like painting or going out for salsa with my friends, because even the thought of doing them feels too exhausting and pointless.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, such as trouble falling asleep or waking up too early, or any changes in your appetite over these past three weeks?

My appetite has completely dropped, and I barely eat during my 12-hour shifts—even my mom's homemade food just tastes like cardboard to me now. I don't really have trouble falling asleep or waking up early, but I'm so exhausted that I usually just mindlessly scroll on the couch until I fall asleep.
Have you found it harder than usual to concentrate, focus, or make decisions recently, especially during your shifts at the clinic?

Yes, my brain feels foggy all the time, and I've actually been making more charting errors at the clinic because I keep losing track of what patients are telling me. I also find myself staring at my study guides without absorbing anything, and even a simple decision like what to wear to work can leave me frozen for ten minutes.
You mentioned things got much worse three weeks ago. Were you already experiencing some of these feelings of depression, exhaustion, or low mood before you found out about the exam result?

Before the exam, I was feeling a lot of stress and pressure from the understaffed clinic, but I was still trying to cope using my usual outlets like painting and yoga. It was only after I got the failed exam result three weeks ago that everything crashed, and these severe feelings of depression, exhaustion, and dark thoughts completely took over.
Have you ever experienced a period in your life before this where you felt this depressed, exhausted, and hopeless for two weeks or more?
No, I've never felt like this before. This is the first time in my life that I've ever felt this depressed, exhausted, and hopeless. I have never experienced anything like this in the past.
Have you or those around you noticed that you are moving, thinking, or speaking much slower than usual, or on the other hand, feeling unusually restless and unable to sit still?

Yes, my coworkers have noticed that I'm moving and speaking much slower, and walking or charting feels like I'm wading through mud. It takes me a long time to answer even simple questions because I feel so physically and mentally slowed down. I definitely don't feel unusually restless, though.
Have you been experiencing strong feelings of worthlessness or excessive, inappropriate guilt over the past three weeks, perhaps feeling like you are to blame for things outside your control?

Yes, I feel completely useless and hollow almost every day now. After I failed that exam, I interpreted it as absolute proof that I am failing both my patients and my long-term goals, and I just feel like a complete failure.
To help me rule out other potential causes, do you have any medical conditions, like thyroid issues, or are you taking any medications or substances that might be contributing to these symptoms?
No, I don't have any medical conditions like thyroid issues that I'm aware of. I'm also not taking any medications or using any substances that could be causing these feelings.
